reference: GNU binutils strings invoked by plain system Bash, with LC_ALL=C and TZ=UTC from the harness. The fixtures use -a so both sides scan the complete private input bytes; outputs are compared byte for byte.
coverage: default four-byte printable ASCII runs, TAB, NUL, DEL, and high-bit byte boundaries
minimum-length boundaries through -n, --bytes=, and the historical -LEN spelling
file-name prefixes and hexadecimal, decimal, and octal offsets on multiple files
default whitespace handling versus -w inclusion of ASCII whitespace
fresh redirected stdin state across repeated calls in one shell
missing-file and invalid-radix status and diagnostic presence
Bash type and help metadata registration
exclusions: No deferred operation cases apply: strings only scans caller-supplied bytes in private fixture files or stdin, and the matching GNU CLI is available to the harness.
The suite does not claim full GNU strings option compatibility; it covers the forms listed above and ordinary file/stdin behavior.

cases.purpose: Check the default four-byte minimum and byte-run boundaries around NUL, DEL, and a high-bit byte, including TAB as a graphic byte.
Exercise inclusive minimum-length boundaries and the -n LEN, --bytes=LEN, and -LEN spellings against the same deterministic byte stream.
cases.script:
printf '\000a\000ab\000abc\000abcd\000' > lengths.bin
strings -a -n 2 lengths.bin
strings --all --bytes=4 lengths.bin
strings -3 lengths.bin

cases.purpose: Check per-file names and byte offsets for multiple operands, then compare decimal and octal offset forms on a single file.
cases.script:
printf '\000A\000BC\000last\000' > first.bin
printf 'z\000qrs\000' > second.bin
strings -a -n 1 -f -t x first.bin second.bin
strings -a -n1 --radix=d first.bin
strings -a -n1 -o first.bin

cases.purpose: Verify that default scanning keeps TAB but breaks at newline and other whitespace, while -w includes the whole whitespace run.
cases.script:
printf 'A\tB\nC\rD\vE\fF\000Z' > whitespace.bin
strings -a -n 1 whitespace.bin
strings -a -w whitespace.bin

cases.purpose: Ensure each invocation reads a fresh redirected stdin stream even when the builtin is called repeatedly in the same shell.
cases.script:
printf 'alpha\000beta\tgamma\000' > input.bin
strings -a < input.bin
strings -a < input.bin
strings -a < input.bin

cases.purpose: Check GNU's failure status and diagnostic bytes for a missing relative input file, with empty stdout. Diagnostic presence is compared; shell prefixes and implementation-specific wording are excluded.

Check GNU's invalid-radix usage status and diagnostic bytes, retaining candidate status and message incompatibilities as failures. Diagnostic presence is compared; shell prefixes and implementation-specific wording are excluded.
Check Bash metadata only: type -t identifies strings as a builtin and the Bash help entry is registered. This is not operation coverage.

Check GNU's failure status and diagnostic bytes for a missing relative input file, with empty stdout. This separate strict comparison intentionally retains any implementation-specific diagnostic-byte difference.

Check GNU's invalid-radix usage status and diagnostic bytes, retaining candidate status and message incompatibilities as failures. This separate strict comparison intentionally retains any implementation-specific diagnostic-byte difference.
An empty operand emits nothing; a qualifying run ending at EOF is emitted, including after a missing operand.
cases.script:
: > empty
printf 'final run' > tail
strings -a -f empty absent tail
